assumptions: The initial target is limited to commercial owners and demolition contractors with recurring pipelines of substantial projects, not small one-off demolition sites.

The service can contract with a licensed operator of record and insured specialists, but that arrangement does not automatically remove the service's own lot-specific product, waste, BDO, or liability duties.
No paid retainer, reliable gate performance, buyer liquidity, contribution margin, or exclusive portfolio access is assumed beyond the evidence in the packet.
The founder can remain part-time during pilot validation but would add dedicated operations capacity before attempting material project throughput.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A paid multi-site retainer from a Polish anchor customer; retrospective and then live results across at least twenty representative sites showing screening cost, gate accuracy, recoverable value, removal cost, sale completion, and contribution margin; repeat buyer demand within economical transport distance; and a written legal, insurance, and operator-of-record contract model for the initial component classes.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: Screening a recurring project pipeline before expensive audits or waste classification closes the reuse option is a coherent control point. The value-to-delivery-cost gate directly addresses a known failure mode, although the insight is operationally intuitive and readily imitated.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Waste separation, demolition planning, and avoiding uneconomic recovery work create a credible owner and contractor problem. However, paid audits are not generally mandated, the economic benefit is uncertain, and no Polish customer evidence establishes willingness to pay a recurring screening retainer.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: A retainer plus gated audit fee is more resilient than relying only on marketplace commissions, and passing specialist costs through could protect margin. The decisive variables—retainer price, screening effort, gate pass rate, audit margin, completed-sale rate, CAC, retention, payback, and owner earnings—are all unknown, while low lot values and specialist-heavy delivery can erase contribution.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Polish commercial portfolios and demolition contractors with substantial recurring projects form a focused, logically selected beachhead. Its economically serviceable volume is not evidenced, and narrowing to pre-sellable non-structural components may leave too few gate-passing sites or too little recoverable value.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: Controlling the portfolio review before procurement could create privileged project access. Yet Concular already offers nearly the full proposed workflow, substitutes can list inventory cheaply or without commission, and the candidate has no exclusive supply, buyer network, or anchor relationship from which to dominate the Polish niche.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: Successful portfolio data and partner workflows could extend into more component classes, compliance and decision software, additional owners, and nearby geographies. Expansion remains conditional on proving local liquidity and lawful, profitable delivery before taking on structurally riskier materials.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Paired screening, removal, acceptance, and outcome data could improve triage and quoting, while recurring portfolio integration may add switching friction. Those advantages start from zero, can be replicated by incumbents with more projects, and may be weakened by a public European pre-demolition data platform.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: The gate promises customers lower wasted audit spend and a single decision process without forcing the venture to hold inventory or regulated waste. No measured comparison shows materially better cost, recovery yield, speed, liability, or convenience than in-house triage, a demolition contractor, or an incumbent full-stack service.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: Poland's 2025 separation duties and broader EU circular-construction policy support attention and inventory formation. Momentum is moderated by non-binding audit guidance, uncertain economics, route-specific regulation, and prospective public infrastructure that could commoditize inventory data.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: A small number of portfolio owners, contractors, architects, and licensed operators offers a more concentrated and repeatable route than an open marketplace. Access, sales-cycle length, channel incentives, portfolio exclusivity, and customer acquisition cost remain untested, and established contractors may internalize the screening or choose an incumbent.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: The founder's data and AI skills fit screening and evidence systems, and a pilot can fit the stated capital if field work is delegated. Each live project still combines legal classification, hazardous-material, testing, title, schedule, removal, storage, transport, insurance, and buyer coordination risks; deadline-sensitive exception handling makes meaningful scale incompatible with a solo part-time operation.

highest_value_structural_change: Make a licensed demolition or waste operator the embedded channel and prime field contractor, while the venture supplies the portfolio-gating decision system under a multi-site annual minimum and advances a lot only after buyer demand is precommitted; this would tie distribution, compliant delivery, and revenue to existing project flow instead of speculative transaction liquidity.
main_structural_strength: The recurring portfolio control point and conservative pre-audit gate align payment with an owner decision while avoiding inventory ownership and filtering out sites whose likely salvage value cannot cover specialist delivery costs.
primary_score_limiter: There is no evidence yet that the central loop works economically: customers pay a recurring retainer, early data predict worthwhile sites, enough lots sell locally, and completed projects retain attractive contribution after specialist and coordination costs.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Concular already combines audits, digital inventory, marketplace distribution, logistics, and insured or warranted installation, directly weakening claims of a distinctive workflow or an open path to a dominant position.
